Subject: SDK kickoff + local run: auth, routing, structured output checklist

Thanks for the call today — good initial signal on fit. Quick recap and proposed immediate next steps so your engineering team can validate locally before we propose a Dedicated pilot:

1) Goal: get a local sample app running (Python + TS) that demonstrates: authenticated calls, request routing to a reranker, structured-tool calls (simple tool/suite), and embeddings for semantic search.
2) Deliverables we attached: a one-page SDK_quickstart_checklist.pdf and the sampleapp README we talked through.
3) Ask of Skyward: confirm whether you prefer API-key based auth for the first pass or if you need mTLS/VPC-only access (we can support both). Also let us know if the sample app needs to run behind your VPN.

I'll loop in Marissa (SDK samples) and Priyom (onramp/tooling) — next email will be a short tech checklist you can hand to your infra lead.

—Mateo

Hi Elena — attaching the quick links & minimal runbook. High level checklist for the infra handoff (this mirrors the PDF attached to Mateo's note):

- Clone repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/tree/main/quickstart (Python & TS directories)
- Local prerequisites: Node 18+, Python 3.11, yarn or npm, pipenv/venv optional
- Env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY (dev key), REDWOOD_ENDPOINT (defaults to hosted), REDWOOD_ROUTER_RULES (optional JSON string for routing rules), EMBEDDING_BATCH=16
- Ports: outbound 443 to api.redwood-hosted.com; for Dedicated/VPC pilot we will provide private endpoint.
- Run commands (examples):
  - TS: cd quickstart/ts && yarn install && yarn dev (starts sample UI + server)
  - PY: cd quickstart/py && pip install -r requirements.txt && python app.py (simple CLI + HTTP test harness)

Embeddings/reranker note: our recommended pattern for your use case is to compute user/document embeddings via the embeddings endpoint, store vectors in your DB, and call a fast reranker model with the top-k candidates (we include a minimal reranker flow in sampleapp). Batch size default is 16 for CPU-bound test runs; we'll recommend quantized models if you move to Dedicated.

Attachments: sampleapp-README.md

I'll follow up with a tiny network-ports.csv with exact FQDNs for security. Happy to hop on a 30-min infra walkthrough if helpful — Mateo, can you propose a slot?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Developer Experience, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@skywardhealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK kickoff + local run: auth, routing, structured output checklist

Quick tech clarifications from the onramp side:

- API key for dev: generate from the console and paste into REDWOOD_API_KEY. Keys can be scoped (models, embeddings) if you want least-privilege.
- For routing: REDWOOD_ROUTER_RULES accepts a small JSON that maps route names to model variants; we include a sample in quickstart/quick-router.json. Example: {"rerank": "m-re-ranker-v1", "generate": "redwood-1.3"}.
- Structured tool-calling: sampleapp demonstrates a toy \"calendar-create\" tool (HTTP webhook) invoked via structured output. The SDK supports declarative tool schemas — use them to validate tool args.
- Local mocking: to avoid outbound traffic while testing, run the bundled mock-server (quickstart/mock) which emulates token streaming and KV cache responses.

Security note: if you need VPC-only for the pilot we'll standby to provide private endpoints + a short network diagram. If you want mTLS earlier, we can provision certs via our onboarding flow but that adds ~2 business days to initial setup.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Product Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
